import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/dogs_zurich.csv')

# Create a figure with multiple subplots for comprehensive visualization
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(14, 12))

# 1. Top 10 Most Popular Dog Breeds
ax1 = axes[0, 0]
breed_counts = df['Rasse1Text'].value_counts().head(10)
colors = sns.color_palette("husl", 10)
bars = ax1.barh(range(len(breed_counts)), breed_counts.values, color=colors)
ax1.set_yticks(range(len(breed_counts)))
ax1.set_yticklabels(breed_counts.index)
ax1.invert_yaxis()
ax1.set_xlabel('Number of Registrations')
ax1.set_title('Top 10 Most Popular Dog Breeds in Zurich', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
for i, v in enumerate(breed_counts.values):
    ax1.text(v + 50, i, str(v), va='center', fontsize=9)

# 2. Dog Registrations by District (Kreis)
ax2 = axes[0, 1]
district_counts = df.groupby('KreisLang')['AnzHunde'].sum().sort_values(ascending=True)
colors2 = sns.color_palette("viridis", len(district_counts))
ax2.barh(district_counts.index, district_counts.values, color=colors2)
ax2.set_xlabel('Total Dog Registrations')
ax2.set_title('Dog Registrations by District', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')

# 3. Dog Age Distribution
ax3 = axes[1, 0]
# Get latest year data to avoid counting same dog multiple times
latest_year = df['StichtagDatJahr'].max()
df_latest = df[df['StichtagDatJahr'] == latest_year]
age_dist = df_latest['AlterVHundLang'].value_counts()
# Sort by age numerically
age_order = df_latest.groupby('AlterVHundLang')['AlterVHundSort'].first().sort_values()
age_dist = age_dist.reindex(age_order.index)
age_dist = age_dist.dropna()

colors3 = sns.color_palette("coolwarm", len(age_dist))
ax3.bar(range(len(age_dist)), age_dist.values, color=colors3)
ax3.set_xticks(range(len(age_dist)))
ax3.set_xticklabels(age_dist.index, rotation=45, ha='right', fontsize=8)
ax3.set_xlabel('Dog Age Group')
ax3.set_ylabel('Number of Dogs')
ax3.set_title(f'Dog Age Distribution ({latest_year})', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')

# 4. Dog Gender Distribution by Owner Gender
ax4 = axes[1, 1]
gender_cross = pd.crosstab(df_latest['SexLang'], df_latest['SexHundLang'])
gender_cross.plot(kind='bar', ax=ax4, color=['#FF6B6B', '#4ECDC4', '#95E1D3'])
ax4.set_xlabel('Owner Gender')
ax4.set_ylabel('Number of Dogs')
ax4.set_title('Dog Gender by Owner Gender', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax4.legend(title='Dog Gender', loc='upper right')
ax4.set_xticklabels(ax4.get_xticklabels(), rotation=0)

# Add overall title
fig.suptitle('Dog Registration Analysis in Zurich, Switzerland', 
             fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', y=1.02)

# Adjust layout
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
